prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the clearest case on the shortlist of a general method that changed how chemists everywhere build a bond. Aryl amines went from a forcing, substrate-limited transformation to a routine, predictable step, through ligand design (bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphines) and a mechanistic picture of amine binding, deprotonation and reductive elimination. Its adoption is visible in medicinal and process chemistry, in materials, and in countless total syntheses, and it has been independently confirmed for about thirty years. The attribution is also unusually clean: Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the catalytic, ligand-controlled version, which gives a natural two-person prize with a concise citation.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki), so the committee could reasonably say the principle is recognised and this is an incremental extension to a new bond type. Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide coupling is a real precursor, so an unqualified citation can be contested on priority. Finally, the mature, synthesis-centred nature of the work makes it look conservative next to the newer modalities (degraders, lipid delivery) that have had more visible effects on medicine.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B004 third and sees it as a high-impact, mechanistically understood prize case, but is concerned about overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize and about Kosugi's precursor work.
responses.response: I take the overlap concern seriously but I do not think it holds. The 2010 prize rewarded C-C bond formation with organometallic partners. C-N coupling needed a different mechanistic solution: amine binding, deprotonation, and C-N reductive elimination, which is difficult, plus a new ligand toolbox to suppress beta-hydride elimination and catalyst deactivation. That ligand work is what was new, and it is not a corollary of the 2010 work. On Kosugi, the tin-amide reaction needed stoichiometric toxic tin reagents and had narrow scope. The general, direct amine version is what chemists use, so I would credit Buchwald and Hartwig and mention the precursor in the citation text at most.

responses.point: Linke places Car-Parrinello first because of a clear unifying principle, an unambiguous two-author credit, and four decades of impact at the physics-chemistry border.
responses.response: I agree that B021 has the cleanest attribution of anything on the list, and I would not oppose it. But the qualities Heiner stresses, a unifying principle and clean credit, are matched by B004, and a practical difference matters to me: B004 is used daily by thousands of bench chemists, while the Lagrangian scheme is mostly used by specialists, and much of the ab initio simulation field has since moved to other schemes. I would not call B021 a weaker science case, but I keep B004 ahead on breadth of adoption in molecule-making. I am open to B021 as the physical-chemistry prize in a later year.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B040 first as a game-changer in real-world consequences, with simple, decisive lipid chemistry, and also ranks B004 fourth as a mature industrial method with the 2010 precedent.
responses.response: I agree that the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid is a good design principle and I rank B040 as an alternative. My reservation is attribution: six credited names for a formulation-and-process technology, with the lipid discovery, formulation and combinatorial lipidoid threads separated across Vancouver and Anderson and Langer's work. Any three-person selection will be disputed and will exclude people with strong claims. B004 has no such problem. The 2023 Medicine prize does not remove the case for B040, but the committee should not take the fact that the delivery chemistry went unrecognised in 2023 as a reason to rush the attribution.

responses.point: Aili ranks B046 first as a new chemical modality that turns small molecules into proximity inducers, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the credited trio.
responses.response: The mechanism-to-tool story is real and I rank B046 as my first alternative. As a synthetic chemist I ask what was new chemically, and here the answer is a design concept (induced proximity) rather than a new reaction or synthetic strategy. The proof of clinical benefit is also not yet complete, as Daniel himself notes: there is no approved designed degrader, and the PROTAC versus molecular-glue credit division is unresolved. That makes B046 look a few years early to me, whereas B004 carries no such risk.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the 2010 cross-coupling prize as a bar to a second Pd cross-coupling prize or as an enabling precedent.
Whether a two-part configuration (B004 plus a second achievement) would be preferred, given that the three-name cap makes that awkward when B004 already carries two names.
How the committee wants to handle Kosugi's credited precursor work, in the citation or by omission.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I have no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi (my mentor was Masamune, and my institutions were Chalmers, KTH and Lund); I am a synthetic chemist who uses this chemistry, which is an affinity but not a recusal issue.
